source.title: Exploring the common principal subspace of deep features in neural networks
source.authors: Haoran Liu; Haoyi Xiong; Ya-Qing Wang; Haozhe An; D. Dou; Dong-Rui Wu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures correlations between data-feature principal-subspace angles and model accuracy, but does not test any of the eight specified versions, which concern memorization, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on common subspaces across architectures and learning paradigms and their convergence during training, but those findings do not bear on the specified versions. The relevant results are correlations between angles and training or test accuracy; the paper does not directly measure training-test error gaps.
record.test_reason: The study's principal-subspace correlations do not test V1–V8. Section 4.3 evaluates generalization-gap predictors, including a sharpness baseline, but does not identify that baseline as magnitude-aware sharpness or establish V7's specified comparisons and training conditions.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase accurately summarizes the accuracy-prediction conclusion, but omits the principal finding: models trained on the same dataset share similar principal subspaces across architectures and learning paradigms, with alignment developing during training. The authors also demonstrate generalization-gap prediction using training-data P-vectors. Their assertion that test-accuracy correlations are uniformly stronger than training-accuracy correlations is contradicted by Figures 9–10.
record.recipe_differences: Measures principal-subspace angles and their correlations with accuracy; it does not use the interventions or measures specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlation significance varies by model and accuracy measure: the training-accuracy correlation for PreActResNet-110 on CIFAR-100 is not significant, while its test-accuracy correlation is significant.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-data P-vector angles correlate negatively with training and test accuracy in Figures 9–10. Eleven correlations are significant at 0.05; PreActResNet-110 training accuracy is not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment between raw-data and learned-feature principal subspaces tracks image-classifier accuracy in the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports generalization-gap prediction scores of 3.325 for P-vector angles, 10.667 for an unspecified sharpness baseline, and 15.618 for pseudo-validation accuracy combined with P-vector angles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data principal-subspace angles can complement other predictors of generalization gaps.

record.problems: The study reports correlations rather than causal effects and does not directly measure training-test error gaps. The paper notes one non-significant correlation; most displayed accuracy correlations are reported with coefficients and p-values.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant rows omitted. Other reported P-vector comparisons and convergence results concern shared representation subspaces rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Held-out error comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited and broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, underfitting, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps within a convolutional family at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says the study does not directly evaluate generalization gaps: Section 4.3 and Table 1 evaluate predictors against ground-truth gaps. This still does not establish a test of V7 because the sharpness definition and required comparison conditions are unspecified. Row states above refer to the supplied claim versions; the reported correlations remain valid findings outside those versions.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its comparison to norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.
